newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: More Uzbek pilgrims going to Mecca - paper.
newsitem.headline: More Uzbek pilgrims going to Mecca - paper.

text.p: Over 3,000 Uzbeks will visit Mecca this year to make the "haj", or Moslem pilgrimage, which was banned in Soviet times, a newspaper said on Friday.
Since independence from Moscow in 1991, over 10,000 pilgrims from Uzbekistan have made the haj, the regional weekly Central Asian Post said.
Islam teaches its followers to travel to the holy sites in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, once during their lifetime and millions of Moslems from all over the world flood the Gulf state each year.
But under officially atheist communism, the haj was effectively banned for Uzbeks and for millions of other Moslems across the Soviet Union.
The weekly said that in Soviet times only 20 pilgrims from Uzbekistan's 23 million population had been allowed each year to make the haj.
"The (present) government has supported them (the pilgrims) by establishing an agency that organises tours to the Arabian peninsula," it said.
The national air carrier, Uzbekiston Havo Yullari, has established a special flight schedule to take the pilgrims to Saudi Arabia's port town of Jeddah.

But while allowing the construction of hundreds of mosques since independence, leaders of the Central Asian states -- most of them ex-Communist Party bosses -- are nervous of militant Islam in neighbouring Afghanistan and Iran.
